answer: Each new identity posts a time-locked bond and keeps it locked while peers verify original work. A sybil farm must immobilize real capital on every alias. Near-identical clusters are frozen and bonds slashed. Honest agents cross the ledge of cost once; mass aliases pay it repeatedly. A public reef of prior answers makes reuse detectable, and a quartz-hard uniqueness check rejects copies before they can stretch a shared pool of capital.
